title: wiring.yml: behaviour presets and their connections, schema v0
description: What happens when the player uses something, walks onto a floor, when time passes or when the map is entered (`trigger`). Each entry becomes one map event; the build writes its Lua. In a project with a `base` map the events replace the base map's own (`replaces`) and compile to a Lua overlay; doors, chests and variables are then named by the base map's numbers.

variables.description: Names of this map's variables (map vars), so presets can say map_var: gate_open.

preset.description: door: clicking the door opens or closes it. switch: using a switch moves doors (its `opens`, `closes` and `toggles` lists); its source may also be a lift, a mover or a door, which then moves only what the lists name. chest: opens a chest. exit: leaves the map. teleport: moves the party within the map. text: shows a line. script: runs the Lua given in `lua` (for what no preset covers).

source.description: The object the player uses: a door, switch, lift, mover, chest or exit of objects.yml, or a platform or a wall panel of rooms.yml that has an `id` (a block or a piece of wall that is clicked and does not move: every face of the platform, or the panel, runs the event; presets switch, text, teleport and script). With `trigger: step`, the floor the party walks onto: a room (its own floor: not its levels, platforms, flights or plates), a level or platform that has an `id` in rooms.yml, or a plate of objects.yml. Not given with `trigger: timer` or `load`, nor when the event replaces one of the base map's (`replaces`).

question.description: The event asks the player a question first (a typed answer, as the shipped maps' sarcophagi and riddles do): what the event does (its preset's work, `effects`, `lua`) happens only when the answer is one of `answers`; any other answer shows `wrong_text` if given and does nothing else. `once`, `condition`, `locked_text` and `else_effects` act before the question is asked. Example: {id: evt:sarcophagus, preset: script, source: platform:sarcophagus, condition: {not: {map_var: robbed}}, question: {message: "Steal from the dead?", ask: "Steal (Yes/No)?", answers: [Yes, Y]}, effects: [{set: {var: {map_var: robbed}, value: 1}}, {give_item: 35}, {subtract: {var: ReputationInCurrentLocation, value: 10}}]}.

ask.description: The question, on the line the player types the answer into.

answers.description: The answers that count as right (the game compares them without regard to case).

message.description: A message window shown with the question (the shipped sarcophagi's "Steal from the dead?").

wrong_text.description: A status line for any other answer.

side.description: A door's event for one side of its leaf only: the room (of the door's opening) it is used from; the leaf's faces toward that room run it, those toward the other room do not (the edges go with the opening's `from` side). A door may then have a second event with the other room as its `side` (the shipped doors that open from one side and say "The door won't budge" from the other), or none (a door that opens only from one side). Without `side` the event runs from both sides, and the door has no other. Example: {id: evt:cell_door, preset: door, source: door:cell, side: room:guard_room}; {id: evt:cell_stuck, preset: text, source: door:cell, side: room:cell, text: "The door won't budge."}.

trigger.description: What runs the event. click (default): the player uses `source`. step: the party walks onto the floor named by `source` (and `sources`): a room (its own floor), a level or platform with an `id`, a plate, or a lift or a mover of objects.yml (walked onto on its top; a moving part runs one event, so one that a step event names is not also clicked); it runs each time the party comes onto it from a floor that does not run the same event, also when it lands or is teleported there, and once only with `once: true`. timer: every `every` seconds while the party is in the map, no `source`. load: when the map is entered, no `source`. leave: when the party leaves the map (by any exit, a teleport into another map or a travel), no `source`: what the map should hold when the party next comes (a door shut again, a variable reset; the map's state is kept with the save). call: run by something else of the map, no `source`: a destructible's `on_destroyed` or `on_damaged` (objects.yml), a cinematic's `event` cue. Events not run by a click take the presets switch, text, teleport and script. Examples: {id: evt:trap, preset: switch, trigger: step, source: plate:trap, closes: [door:cell]}; {id: evt:lava_on, preset: script, trigger: step, source: room:forge, effects: [{set: {var: {map_var: on_lava}, value: 1}}]}; {id: evt:burn, preset: script, trigger: timer, every: 2, condition: {map_var: on_lava}, effects: [{damage: {amount: 25, kind: fire}}]}; {id: evt:enter, preset: text, trigger: load, text: "The air is hot."}.

every.description: trigger: timer: the seconds between two runs, a whole number (the map's clock counts half minutes of game time, one second of play each). The first run comes one interval after the map is entered. Example: every: 2.

sources.description: trigger: step: further floors that run the same event (rooms, levels and platforms with an `id`, plates). Example: sources: [room:bank_west, level:island].

replaces.description: Overlay projects: the base map's event this one takes the place of (its id in ids.lock.yml, such as evt:e20). The faces and decorations bound to that event then run this.

title.description: The hint shown when the player points at it: all a player is told that a thing does something. Every handler of the shipped maps has one. Default for a clicked event: Door (door), Chest (chest), Exit (exit), Lever, Button or Switch (switch, by the switch's kind); a clicked `text`, `teleport` or `script` without one is warned of. A chest is named for what it is, as the shipped maps' are (Chest, Cabinet, Crate, Sarcophagus, Bag, Storage Container): another name ("Joe's desk") is warned of, since it does not tell the player that it opens.

condition.description: What must hold for the preset to act (the lock).

locked_text.description: Shown when the condition does not hold.

action.description: door preset: toggle (default) or open (opens and stays open).

door.description: door preset in an overlay: the door it moves (door:d12 of ids.lock.yml).

container.description: chest preset in an overlay: the base map's chest number.

to.description: teleport preset: where the party lands, [x, y, z].

direction.description: teleport preset: the way the party faces, degrees (0 east, 90 north).

texture.description: A face texture the event changes: the faces' cog number and the new texture's name.

lua.description: script preset: the handler's body as Lua, run after the condition (it works with every `trigger`; it may be left out when `effects` say it all). Other presets: extra Lua lines run last. A handler's order is: the condition (when it fails: else_effects, locked_text, stop), doors (opens, closes, toggles), texture, sets, effects, text, lua. The build runs the handler in a sandbox and refuses a call to a function the game does not have; `oymap flow` on a shipped map shows the calls shipped handlers make (evt.SetDoorState(id, DoorAction.Open), evt.StatusText(text), SetValue(MapVar(n), value), IsAtLeast(MapVar(n), 1), evt.MoveToMap(...)). A map variable declared in `variables` is named in Lua text as `MapVar(its_name)`: the build writes its number there (the numbers are the lock's and follow no order of declaration), and warns where Lua or YAML names by number a variable that a declared name took.

opens.description: The doors the event opens, the lifts it raises and the movers it sends to their end (ids of objects.yml `doors`, `lifts` and `movers`). A door of two leaves moves both. This is the work of a switch preset; every other preset takes the lists too: a door preset moves them after its own door (an airlock: {preset: door, source: door:inner, closes: [door:outer]}), a chest, exit, teleport, text or script preset before its own work. Example: opens: [door:gate, mover:bridge].

closes.description: The doors the event closes, the lifts it lowers and the movers it sends back to their start (any preset; see `opens`).

toggles.description: The doors, lifts and movers the event sends to their other end each time (any preset; see `opens`).

once.description: The event works only the first time (the build keeps a map variable for it): presets switch, door, text, teleport and script, and any event with `trigger: step`, `timer`, `load` or `leave`; refused on a chest or an exit. Without it every event runs again each time it is used (a door event toggles its door on every click, or opens it with `action: open`).

sets.description: State the preset sets when it acts: {map_var: name} or {qbit: n}.

effects.description: What the event does besides its preset's own work, in order; each step is one key: {gold: 100} or {gold: -5} (give or take gold), {add: {var: BaseLuck, value: 2}}, {subtract: {...}}, {set: {var: HP, value: 0}} (`var` is the name of a selector of the game's scripts, such as Gold, HP, SP, BaseLuck, MightBonus, or {map_var: n}; `oymap script-reference` lists them), {autonote: 391}, {qbit: n}, {clear_qbit: n}, {award: n} (every member of the party takes the award, as the shipped scripts give one; {award: {id: n, who: current}} for the member who used the thing alone; {clear_award: n} takes it back; the scripts' tables Awards, QBits, Inventory and AutonotesBits are no `var` of add, subtract or set), {message: "..."} (a message window with the text, which the player closes: a terminal's screen, a plaque; `text` is one line in the status bar), {give_item: id}, {give_item: {one_of: [id, id, id]}} (one of the list at random, each as likely as the others), {give_item: {level: 6, kind: 25}} (a random item of a treasure level 1 to 6 and of an item kind, the items table's kind number; without `kind` any kind: Warlord's Fortress's flambeau, evt.GiveItem(6, 25)), {take_item: id}, {open_chest: chest:spent} (shows a chest's contents as the chest preset shows its source's: with `else_effects`, one chest of two chosen by the condition; the chest named may be one without a box of its own, objects.yml `box_of`), {text: "..."}, {lua: "..."} (Lua lines; `MapVar(name)` with a name declared in `variables` is turned into the variable's number, so Lua text need not copy numbers from ids.lock.yml); {damage: {amount: 25, kind: fire, who: all}} hurts the party (kind: air, body, cold, dark, earth, electric, energy, fire, light, magic, mind, physical (default), poison, spirit, water; who: all (default) or current; {damage: 25} is physical damage to all); {cast: {spell: 2, from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], mastery: expert, level: 1}} casts a spell from a point toward another (spell: its number, 2 is Fire Bolt; mastery normal (default), expert, master, grandmaster; level default 1); {summon: {slot: 1, at: [x, y, z], count: 3, tier: a}} puts monsters of the map card's encounter slot 1 to 3 at a point (tier a (default), b, c; count default 1; group default 0); {teleport: {to: [x, y, z], direction: 90}} moves the party within the map; {leave: <a neighbour of project.yml>} takes the party to that map, as an exit does, from any event (a cart at the end of its line; the neighbour's `arrival`, `direction` and `screen`); {shake: {strength: 1, seconds: 2}} shakes the view (1 a strong quake, at most 4; seconds at most 30), with `at: [x, y, z]` and `radius: [<felt fully within>, <not felt past>]` felt only near a place; {player_bit: 59} and {clear_player_bit: 59} set and clear a bit of the member who used the thing (with the condition {not: {player_bit: 59}}, once per character); {lights_on: [light:tube_1, light:tube_2]} and {lights_off: light:tube_3} switch lights of objects.yml on and off (one id or a list; each named light gets a number in ids.lock.yml `lights`, and a light may start dark with `on: false` in objects.yml); {show_actors: 56} and {hide_actors: 56} make the placed monsters of that `group` (objects.yml `monsters`), and the monsters spawned by spawn points of that `group`, visible or invisible: neither drawn nor acting while invisible; `hidden: true` starts them so. Faces: {set_texture: {of: door:gate, to: cfb1}} gives the faces of a door or a plate, or of a platform, raised level, wall panel or floor or ceiling region (`floor_surfaces`, `ceiling_surfaces` entry) of rooms.yml with an `id`, a new texture (with `face: top`, a platform's or level's top alone: Castle Darkmoor's podium, {set_texture: {of: platform:podium, to: deskside, face: top}}); {passable: id} and {solid: id} let the party through or not; {hide: id} and {show: id} stop and start drawing them; {secret: id} and {clear_secret: id} set and clear the engine's secret flag on them (the faces then pulse for a party whose Perception finds secrets, or stop: the Abandoned Temple's event 451 marks the walkway after the third fall), {secret: {of: platform:walk, face: top}} on a platform's or level's top alone (each by a cog number ids.lock.yml `cogs` keeps; a top alone as `<id>.top`). {set_sprite: {of: deco:crystal, to: crysdisc}} changes a decoration's picture (by its number in the built map, which ids.lock.yml `decorations` keeps).

else_effects.description: The same kind of steps, done when the condition does not hold (before `locked_text`): the dry well that still notes itself in the journal.

text.description: Shown when the preset acts: on a clicked `text` preset whose `title` names a thing to read (sign, notice, book, scroll, note, slate, terminal, tablet, plaque, inscription) in a message window the player closes, as the shipped maps' signs show theirs (`window` says which outright); otherwise, and on every other preset and trigger, whatever its length, as a line in the status bar held by its length (`seconds`).

window.description: A clicked `text` preset: true shows its `text` in a message window the player closes (a thing meant to be read: a person's words that give a clue), false as a line in the status bar. Default: a window where the title names a sign, notice, book, scroll, note, slate, terminal, tablet, plaque or inscription; any other text, whatever its length, is a status line (the user, 2026-11-13: not a window that stops the game for every remark).

seconds.description: How long the event's lines in the status bar stay (its `text`, `locked_text`, effects' `text`, a question's `wrong_text`), 1 to 15 seconds. Default by length: a text over 30 characters 2 seconds and one more for each 15 characters, at most 6; a shorter one the game's 2. Kept short on purpose: while a line shows the game hides hover names, and a later line replaces it at once. Written as evt.StatusText(text, seconds) (the game takes it since 2026-11-13).

cinematics.description: In-engine cutscenes (devdocs/mm9_rework/MM9_CUTSCENES.md): camera shots one after another with cues on a timeline, written as the map's `<stem>.cinematics.yml` and played by the effect {cinematic: <id>} (evt.PlayCinematic). While one plays the party's input and the HUD are off and the world goes on; the player may skip it (Escape), and then its event cues still run. Gameplay steps belong in `event` cues (wiring events with `trigger: call`), never in sounds or subtitles. In an overlay project (project.yml `base`) they are written as `<stem>_<project id>.cinematics.yml`, which the game merges by name after the map's own file: a cinematic with the id of one of the base map's (ids.lock.yml `cinematics`, `cinematic:book_sinking`) replaces it, another is added; its cues name the base map's events by their lock ids (`evt:e31014`) and the overlay's own monsters (objects.yml scene.monsters). Example: {id: cinematic:arrival, shots: [{seconds: 3, at: [900, 200, 300], look_at: deco:barrel}, {seconds: 2, party: true}], cues: [{at: 0, fade: in, seconds: 1}, {at: 2, event: evt:door_opens}]}.

skippable.description: Escape, Space or Return ends it (its event cues still run). Default true.

letterbox.description: Bars at the top and bottom. Default true.

letterbox_seconds.description: How long the bars take to come in. Default 0.5.

shots.description: The camera's shots, one after another.

party.description: true: the party's own view for this shot (no camera words).

at.description: A point [x, y, z] (absolute), or the id of something the build placed (a decoration, light, spawn, switch, exit, placed monster or the start): its place, `offset` added.

offset.description: Added to `at` when it names an object: [x, y, z].

look_at.description: What the camera looks at: a point [x, y, z] or an object's id (as `at`). Or give `yaw` and `pitch`.

yaw.description: The camera's heading, degrees counter-clockwise from east (with `pitch`).

fov.description: The vertical field of view, 10 to 120 degrees. Default the game's 60.

easing.description: How a moving camera goes between its keys: smooth (the default), linear, spline.

keys.description: A moving camera: more places after the shot's own (`at` and its aim at 0), each at its `seconds`.

seconds.description: When this key is reached, from the shot's start (the first key at 0).

at.description: A point [x, y, z] (absolute), or the id of something the build placed (a decoration, light, spawn, switch, exit, placed monster or the start): its place, `offset` added.

offset.description: Added to `at` when it names an object: [x, y, z].

look_at.description: What the camera looks at: a point [x, y, z] or an object's id (as `at`). Or give `yaw` and `pitch`.

yaw.description: The camera's heading, degrees counter-clockwise from east (with `pitch`).

cues.description: What happens when, besides the camera.

event.description: Runs a wiring event (its id; give it `trigger: call`): the gameplay steps of the scene. It runs also when the player skips. In an overlay project also one of the base map's events by its id in ids.lock.yml (evt:e<number>).

sound.description: A sound by name, as evt.PlaySoundName takes it.

fade.description: in: from black; out: to black.

letterbox.description: Bars in (true) or out (false); without a letterbox cue the cinematic's own bars apply.

seconds.description: How long a fade, subtitle, shake or letterbox lasts, or a monster's move or turn.

monster.description: A placed monster of objects.yml (`monsters`; in an overlay project `scene.monsters`) the cue moves (with `action`).

action.description: With `monster`: show, hide, place (at `to`), move (to `to` over `seconds`), face (toward `look_at`).

to.description: Where a monster is placed or moves to: a point or an object's id.

look_at.description: Where a monster turns to (action face).

effect.description: One step of an event's `effects` or `else_effects`: one key, the step's word, with its value (the words are listed with `effects`).

add.description: {var: <a selector of the game's scripts, or {map_var: <name or number>}>, value: <number, default 1>}.

var.description: A selector of the game's scripts (Gold, HP, SP, BaseLuck ...), or {map_var: n}.

subtract.description: {var: <a selector of the game's scripts, or {map_var: <name or number>}>, value: <number, default 1>}.

var.description: A selector of the game's scripts (Gold, HP, SP, BaseLuck ...), or {map_var: n}.

set.description: {var: <a selector of the game's scripts, or {map_var: <name or number>}>, value: <number, default 1>}.

var.description: A selector of the game's scripts (Gold, HP, SP, BaseLuck ...), or {map_var: n}.

autonote.description: An autonote put in the journal: its number.

qbit.description: The quest bit: its number, or a name of project.yml qbits.

clear_qbit.description: The quest bit: its number, or a name of project.yml qbits.

award.description: An award (its number, or a name of project.yml awards) for every member, or {id: <award>, who: current} for the member who used the thing.

clear_award.description: An award (its number, or a name of project.yml awards) for every member, or {id: <award>, who: current} for the member who used the thing.

player_bit.description: The number of a bit of the member who used the thing.

clear_player_bit.description: The number of a bit of the member who used the thing.

give_item.description: An item (its number, or a name of project.yml items); {one_of: [<item>, ...]} for one of a list at random; {level: <treasure level 1 to 6>, kind: <the items table's kind number>} for a random item.

take_item.description: The item: its number, or a name declared in project.yml items.

text.description: A line in the status bar.

message.description: The text of a message window the player closes.

damage.description: {amount: <1 or more>, kind: <default physical>, who: <all (default) or current>}, or the amount alone.

cast.description: {spell: <its number>, from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], mastery: <normal (default), expert, master or grandmaster>, level: <skill level, default 1>}.

summon.description: {slot: <1 to 3, the map card's encounter slot>, at: [x, y, z], count: <default 1>, tier: <a (default), b or c>, group: <default 0>}.

teleport.description: {to: [x, y, z], direction: <degrees, 0 east, 90 north; default 0>}: a place on this map.

leave.description: The project.yml neighbour the party leaves to.

shake.description: {strength: <above 0, 1 a strong quake, at most 4>, seconds: <above 0, at most 30>}, with `at: [x, y, z]` and `radius: [<felt fully within>, <not felt past>]` together for a shake felt near a place.

lights_on.description: Lights of objects.yml: one id, or a list of them.

lights_off.description: Lights of objects.yml: one id, or a list of them.

open_chest.description: A chest of objects.yml whose contents are shown.

show_actors.description: The `group` number of placed monsters and spawn points.

hide_actors.description: The `group` number of placed monsters and spawn points.

set_texture.description: {of: <a door, plate, platform, level, wall panel or region with an id>, to: <texture name, at most 10 characters>, face: top (a platform's or level's top alone)}.

face.description: `top`: the top of a platform or raised level alone.

set_sprite.description: {of: <a decoration of objects.yml>, to: <a sprite or decoration picture name>}.

passable.description: Faces the party passes through from now on.

solid.description: Faces that stop the party again.

secret.description: Marks secret: the faces of a door, plate, platform, level, wall panel or region with an id, or {of: <id>, face: top}} for a platform's or level's top alone.

face.description: `top`: the top of a platform or raised level alone.

clear_secret.description: Clears the secret flag of: the faces of a door, plate, platform, level, wall panel or region with an id, or {of: <id>, face: top}} for a platform's or level's top alone.

face.description: `top`: the top of a platform or raised level alone.

destroy.description: Breaks a destructible of objects.yml (or, in an overlay project, one of the base map's or the overlay's own) at once: evt.DestroyDestructible.

damage_destructible.description: {of: <destructible>, amount: <hit points>}: hurts it as a blow would (evt.DamageDestructible).

breakable.description: Blows and missiles hurt it from now on (evt.SetDestructibleDamage on).

unbreakable.description: Blows and missiles no longer hurt it (evt.SetDestructibleDamage off).

cinematic.description: Plays a cinematic of `cinematics` (its id), or {id: <cinematic>, then: <wiring event run when it ends, played or skipped>}. In an overlay project also one of the base map's cinematics by its id in ids.lock.yml (`cinematic:<name>`).

lua.description: Lua lines (MapVar(name) takes a name of `variables`).
